text: The World Series swings back to American Family Field for Game 2 with Milwaukee holding a 1-0 lead in the best-of-seven. Milwaukee finished the regular season at 103-59, the best record in baseball, and they carry that strength onto their own patch, where the crowd will be at its loudest of the series. Tampa Bay are 98-64 and have to travel all night after dropping Game 1, so fatigue and venue both point the same way. With the series still open and the Brewers needing only two more wins at home, the value sits with the home side. Back Milwaukee Brewers to win Game 2 at -130, a Medium confidence selection for this game.

Chicago carry the softest line in this sample at 3-7-0, which leaves them at the bottom of the NHL standings and leaking goals at home. Florida arrive at United Center with a 5-4-2 record and a sharper forward group, so the Panthers are the better side on the official numbers even though they are on the road. The Blackhawks' own record explains why this line is close rather than wide. Take Florida Panthers to win at -135; that is our Medium confidence call for this meeting.

Dallas sit higher on the official NHL standings with a 6-3-1 line and a home record that has carried them through the early weeks of the season. New York are 5-3-2 and have looked vulnerable away from home, so the Stars hold both the better goaltending and the better structure in this match-up. American Airlines Center is a difficult building for visiting attackers and the Islanders have not shown the consistency needed to take points there. Our Medium confidence view is Dallas Stars to win at -133 on Sunday's late NHL game.

Danil Medvedev is the higher-ranked player and he reached this ATP Almaty final the harder way, beating Alexander Bublik in three sets, 7-5 3-6 6-1, after a break-exchange opening set. Medvedev's serve and his ability to extend rallies from the baseline give him the edge against Nikoloz Basilashvili, who has to generate his own pace and who conceded breaks in both of his matches this week. Basilashvili beat Stefanos Tsitsipas to reach the final, so he is not a free pass, but Medvedev's semi-final win was built on taking control of his own serve. Back Danil Medvedev to win and lift the trophy at -163, a High confidence pick.

Tommy Paul has been the most consistent player on the ATP Lyon draw and he made the final by beating Ben Shelton in straight sets. Lorenzo Musetti reached the title match by beating Flavio Cobolli 6-4 6-2, so both men are playing confident tennis, but Paul's all-court game and his serve-plus-one pattern are harder for Musetti to handle on an indoor hard court. Paul's route to the final has required fewer break points than Musetti's, which points to a more controlled service game. Take Tommy Paul to win at -150 - the desk's High confidence call on this title match.

Jan-Lennard Struff reached this ATP Brussels final by beating Jaume Munar in the semi-finals, while Tallon Griekspoor had to fight past Terence Atmane to take the other side of the draw. Struff's game is built for this match-up: a heavy first serve and a forehand that punishes weak returns. Griekspoor is a solid all-rounder but he has not faced a serve of that quality this week. The gap between them is small enough that the title is genuinely open. Back Jan-Lennard Struff to win at -135, the desk's Medium confidence view on this match-up.

Gerwyn Price reached the PDPA European Championship quarter-final with a 10-8 win over Nathan Aspinall in round two, and Stephen Bunting answered with a 10-6 success against Scott Williams, so both men arrive at Sunday in form. Price is the more proven competitor at this stage of a major and the PDPA draw puts this one in a Sunday afternoon session, which is the stage Price has won on before. Bunting's route has been quieter, which is the kind of run that can catch a stronger opponent cold. Our Medium confidence pick is Gerwyn Price to win at -127.

Ross Smith advanced into his PDPA European Championship quarter-final by beating Michael van Gerwen 10-7 in round two, which tells you his scoring is right at the top of its range against the best player in the draw. Luke Woodhouse replied with a 10-6 win over Dirk van Duivenboe, so he is not an easy opponent, but Smith has faced the harder opponent and still won by three legs. Smith's route has been built on taking his chances when they arrive, and the official PDPA draw has put him on a Sunday stage he has played on before. Take Ross Smith to win at -122, our Medium confidence call on Sunday's session.

Kyren Wilson is the defending Northern Ireland Open champion and he arrives in the final as the stronger of the two players, having won his semi-final without dropping a frame from the interval. His opponent is the winner of the Mark Williams v Jac Jones semi-final, which was level at 5-5 when read, so the final pairing is not settled. Wilson's centuries and his safety play have been the most reliable part of his tournament this week, and the venue is a stage he has already won at. The desk's High confidence pick is Kyren Wilson to win the title at -174.

Pakistan are the home side at Gaddafi Stadium and they have already put England under real pressure in this tri-series, with England 5-0 down across the limited-overs leg. England's batsmen have not converted starts into partnerships in any of the five matches they have lost, and the bowling attack has not been able to restrict Pakistan's top order. Pakistan's batting looks settled and they will want to finish the series at home in Lahore. Pakistan to win at -144 is our Medium confidence view on the third ODI.

Australia meet Fiji in Brisbane with both teams carrying four competition points after winning their opening Rugby League World Cup games. Australia are the stronger side on recent history and on squad strength, and they have the home venue for this one at Suncorp Stadium. Fiji's opening win put them level on points, but the step up in opposition quality is the test here. Take Australia to win at -245: our High confidence pick for this group match.

New Zealand meet the Cook Islands in Christchurch and the home venue alone makes them the side to beat on this evidence. Both teams have two competition points after one group game, but New Zealand's squad is drawn from NRL clubs while the Cook Islands rely on a smaller professional base. New Zealand's opening group game was a win and the question here is only by how much. Back New Zealand to win at -194: the High confidence view in Christchurch.

Antonelli takes the United States Grand Prix into race day on provisional pole with a lap of 1:34.035, the fastest of the weekend at the Circuit of the Americas. The official F1 event page frames Sunday as a 56-lap sprint on the 5.513 kilometre track. Antonelli's qualifying advantage over Verstappen is only a tenth of a second, so the race is far from decided, and the field behind includes Hadjar, Leclerc and Hamilton. That makes the race-winner market a genuine multi-runner and the desk's estimate for Antonelli is only 30%. Back Antonelli to win the race at 233 as a Low confidence outright, not a banker.

The Butterfield Bermuda Championship goes to the final round with Austin Smotherman and Ryan Gerard tied at the top of the leaderboard on 16 under par, two shots clear of Ben Moore, Ben Conners and Brian Silverman on 14 under. Ryan Gerard leads the field in putts made, which is the statistic that converts chances into a trophy on a soft Bermuda green. Smotherman is level with him on total, and with five players inside three shots of the lead the outright is a genuine multi-runner rather than a two-horse race. Take Austin Smotherman to win the tournament at 233 as our Low confidence outright pick.
